questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Carnegie's first jobs and his family's pride and determination
Carnegie's later steel fortune and his gifts to libraries
Carnegie's voyage to America and first weeks in Allegheny
Carnegie's schooling in Scotland and his love of Wallace
questions.explain: Carnegie describes starting work at thirteen to help the family and his mother's pride.

questions.q: How much did Carnegie earn weekly as a bobbin boy at Mr. Blackstock's factory?
options: Two dollars and fifty cents
Twenty-five cents a day
Three dollars and ten cents
One dollar and twenty cents
questions.explain: His first work was at one dollar and twenty cents per week.

questions.q: How did his mother react when her brother-in-law's relative suggested he peddle goods on the wharves?
options: She gladly accepted the offer and bought him a basket
She said she would rather throw him into the Allegheny River
She asked young Andrew to decide whether he wanted it
She suggested he first work as a clerk on the wharves
questions.explain: She declared she would rather throw him into the Allegheny River and sent Mr. Hogan away.

questions.q: What task at Mr. Hay's did Carnegie never get used to?
options: Writing out bills for Mr. Hay, which strained his hands
Firing the boiler in the cellar, which he found too easy
Bathing newly made spools in oil, whose smell made him sick
Running errands across Allegheny City in the cold
questions.explain: He never overcame the nausea from the oil smell.

questions.q: What does Carnegie imply his mother objected to about peddling?
options: It paid too little to help the family reach its goal
It was hard physical labor, which she thought beneath him
It would have kept him from the schooling she valued
It was not respectable and meant mingling with rough company
questions.explain: Her objection was that the work was vagrant and not respectable, not that it was labor.
